newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's spring trucking bans may begin this week.
newsitem.headline: Canada's spring trucking bans may begin this week.

text.p: Bans on grain trucking on rural Prairie roads may come into effect as early as this week, provincial highway departments told Reuters on Monday.
Weight restrictions on Prairie highways are an annual occurence. Roads subjected to winter freezing and spring thawing make surfaces vulnerable to damage from heavy truck traffic.
Limited loads are permitted during the spring thaw.
Alberta may be the first province to institute bans on March 13, followed by Saskatchewan on March 16.
"The earliest would be this Sunday at midnight but I doubt it unless it really warms up," Saskatchewan Highway department spokesman Gary McClelland said in a telephone interview.
Road bans mean a smaller amount of grain can be trucked to primary elevators than at any other time of the crop year.
Manitoba plans to put its first road bans in place on March 23.
